differences.why: Whole numbers. MacroPress has one whole-number type where VBA has Integer and Long: TypeName goes by the number's size, and two Integers whose sum or product passes 32,767 give the number where VBA stops with error 6.
Regional settings. The Mac that recorded Excel's answers reads and writes dates day first; MacroPress follows US settings, month first.
DateDiff. Excel for Mac counts the whole hours and days that have passed; MacroPress counts the hour and day boundaries crossed, as VBA's documentation has it.
UCase of ß. Excel for Mac gives a single S; MacroPress gives SS.
The name of Excel's own short date format. The Mac that recorded the answers names it m/d/yy, by its regional settings; MacroPress names it m/d/yyyy, as NumberFormat does under US settings.
Activating a hidden sheet. Excel for Mac makes it the active sheet; Excel for Windows refuses with error 1004, as MacroPress does, and so a range of it cannot be selected either.
